Subject: MSA + Order Form — confidentiality/publicity clauses

Rafael,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. Legal here — attaching our redline of the MSA and an annotated order form. Two items we need clarity on before we can sign:

1) Publicity/reference rights: we are OK with a customer badge on your customers page but need explicit opt-in for any press releases or case studies. Please confirm Redwood's standard language for customer quotes and logo use, including approval turnaround time and whether you require a mutual review window.

2) Embargo/announcement timing: we typically request a 60-day embargo from contract signature for joint announcements. If Redwood plans to include BrightLayer in any marketing materials prior to signature, that's a hard no.

3) Confidentiality carveouts: our counsel flagged Section 7.2 (permitted disclosures) — specifically, we want stronger guarantees around audit log access and any telemetry data retention. We are also collecting SOC 2 evidence for procurement — please advise what you can provide.

Attaching: BrightLayer_Redline_MSA.docx, BrightLayer_OrderForm_annotated.pdf

Can you confirm next steps and an ETA for legal review on your side?

Regards,

Dana — thanks for the redlines and the clear summary. I will loop in our legal team and product security to confirm the SOC2/evidence items. Quick answers up front:

- Reference & logos: our standard policy is opt-in. We ask for a short approval window (5 business days) for quotes and logos and we don’t publish anything without your signoff. For press releases we allow a mutual review window and can agree to a pre-announcement embargo.
- Embargo: 60 days is reasonable; if we have a product-led brief mention (in list form) we can discuss but we will not publish any case study or quote prior to approval.
- Audit/logs: we can provide SOC2 report summary and scoped audit artifacts via an evidence package; we will confirm what can be shared given customer data constraints.

Kimberly, Marissa — forwarding BrightLayer's legal with their annotated redline. Quick bullets on commercial priorities so legal knows negotiating constraints:

- Customer wants explicit opt-in for press/case studies and 60-day embargo post-signature. We should accept opt-in and the embargo, but push back on any "hard no" language that prevents reference qualification post-signature.
- Logo usage: limit to approved assets and approval window of 5 business days. Do not accept unlimited sublicensing for logos.
- Quotes/attribution: acceptable to require mutual review; suggest we add a clause that text edits for brand safety are allowed but not substantive content changes without partner approval.
- Confidentiality carveouts: they want scope on telemetry/audit logs. Product security: recommend providing SOC2 summary + curated evidence package (no raw logs). Legal: confirm acceptable standard language to commit to evidence delivery timelines (e.g., within 10 business days of request) and any redaction language needed.

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: rafael.mendes@redwood.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com

Team — I reviewed BrightLayer's redline and prepared our tracked changes. Summary and recommended positions below (see attached Redwood_MSA_redline_trackchanges.docx):

1) Publicity / Reference Rights
- Keep opt-in model. Counter-propose: allow Redwood to list the customer name on a public "Customers" page and in short customer lists in marketing materials; any quote, case study, or press release requires written approval. We will provide a 5-business-day review window for logo & quote approvals and a separate 5-business-day review for final PR text.
- Replace any absolute prohibition language with a mutual-approval clause to keep negotiation room.

2) Embargo / Announcement Timing
- Accept 60-day embargo for joint press if BrightLayer requires it, but request carveout allowing Redwood to include BrightLayer in anonymized benchmarks or aggregated listings (no identifying quotes or logos). If they insist on blocking any mention at all, escalate to Commercial.

3) Confidentiality / Evidence Requests
- Do NOT agree to provide raw telemetry or logs. Offer a packaged evidence bundle that includes the SOC2 report, network diagram, and curated artifacts. Propose commitment: evidence available within 10 business days of a formal request under a controlled access process.
- Add redaction language and data minimization clauses to avoid overbroad disclosure.

4) Implementation notes for Order Form
- Add an addendum referencing the marketing/reference process (approval flow, point of contact, allowed assets).
- Add a single-sentence SLA that Redwood will respond to marketing approval requests within the agreed review windows.

Next steps I propose:
- Send them our redline plus a brief cover email summarizing the positions above.
- If they push back on embargo carveouts, Rafael please escalate to Commercial for a trade-off on price/credits.

Attachments: Redwood_MSA_redline_trackchanges.docx, evidence-package.zip
